propositions: A transient GitHub git fetch hang causes subprocess.TimeoutExpired which is converted to SnapshotFetchError and caught by adapter's blanket exception handler, mistakenly classified as a review fault and voted as durable -1.
The spurious -1 vote is recorded in the dedup store, permanently removing the change from backfill reconciliation because reconcile.py pre-filters out changes with existing LLM-Review votes.
A several-second network stall burns the entire 300s git timeout and triggers the vote-bearing path before the outer 1200s review timeout, guaranteeing infra faults become durable votes.

The system already has correct handling for retryable infrastructure faults at a higher layer (app.py, reconcile.py) that abandons without voting and allows backfill retry, but the inner adapter layer is inconsistent with it.
Infrastructure faults must be distinguished from review conclusions so that only the former follow the no-vote abstention path and remain eligible for backfill recovery.
